quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are gliding. The clue is how long the glide lasts before the ending.
quests.explanation: You heard "site": a shorter glide and a tight, quick tongue-tip stop. "Side" stretches the vowel and lets the ending sound soft.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Ignore the final release; listen to how long the vowel is.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /d/; tighten and stop for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Notice the length of the vowel before the last sound.
quests.explanation: "Mate" is clipped short and finishes crisply. "Made" holds the vowel longer and closes softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Duration is the main clue here, not the ending itself.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "cod": the vowel lasted longer and the closure was soft. "Cot" is short and ends abruptly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how long the glide takes before the closure.
quests.explanation: "Code" gives the glide extra time and ends softly. "Coat" is shorter and sharper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Ignore the final release; listen to how long the vowel is.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /d/; tighten and stop for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two words that end at the back of the tongue. Which vowel is longer?
quests.explanation: That was "wig": the vowel lasted slightly longer and the closure was soft. "Wick" is shorter with a crisp, breathy /k/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /ɡ/ lengthens the preceding vowel and is only lightly released; /k/ shortens it and closes with a sharper stop.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ shorten the vowel and close the back of the tongue at once. For /ɡ/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long. Which one is even longer?
quests.explanation: "Feed" stretches the long vowel further and then ends softly. "Feet" cuts the same vowel a bit shorter and ends with a crisp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel and the last sound together.
quests.explanation: The word was "his": a slightly longer vowel and a soft, voiced ending. "Hiss" is shorter and finishes with a sharp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /z/ often loses some voicing, but it never loses the longer vowel before it.
quests.mouthPosition: Cut the vowel short before /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The last sound is subtle. Focus on the vowel length before it.
quests.explanation: "Dog" holds the vowel longer and ends softly. "Dock" is shorter and closes crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The clearest cue is vowel length: longer before /ɡ/, shorter before /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel slightly before /ɡ/ and clip it before /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both short. Which one needs more jaw opening?
quests.explanation: It was "pin": the jaw stayed nearly closed and the sound was thin. "Pen" opens a bit more and sounds clearer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The vowels are close, so listen for jaw opening: /ɪ/ feels tight and closed, /e/ feels a little more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɪ/ with hardly any jaw movement, then drop the jaw a little for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short vowels ending with a soft /d/. Tight or half-open?
quests.explanation: "Hid" is tight, thin and quick. "Head" is fuller, with the jaw half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ sounds fuller and clearer, /ɪ/ sounds thinner and softer.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the lower front teeth in both; only the height of the tongue body changes.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for the vowel's width.
quests.explanation: You heard "ten": the jaw stayed at half-open. "Tan" opens wider and sounds broader.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Judge the vowel length first, then the lips.
quests.explanation: "Shot" is brief and open, with the lips slightly rounded. "Short" holds a longer, rounder vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In British English /ɔː/ is noticeably longer and 'darker' than /ɒ/, and it uses tighter lip rounding. /ɒ/ is short and more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɒ/ with a dropped jaw and a short beat; say /ɔː/ with rounder lips and a longer, steady vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are open vowels. Which lasts longer?
quests.explanation: That was "heart": the mouth opened wide and stayed there. "Hot" is short, with a more rounded mouth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is short with a rounded lip shape; /ɑː/ is long with the jaw opened wide and the lips neutral. Length and lip shape both help, and /ɑː/ lasts about twice as long.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɑː/ drop the jaw fully and keep the lips flat. For /ɒ/ open less and round the lips slightly, and end the vowel sooner.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowels are equally long, so the lips are your only clue.
quests.explanation: "Bored" has rounded lips and a darker vowel. "Bird" has loose lips and a neutral centre.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ sounds neutral and central; /ɔː/ sounds dark and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips in a mirror: they should stay still for /ɜː/ and round for /ɔː/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short and dull, or long and rounded?
quests.explanation: The word was "cut": short, with neutral lips. "Caught" holds a longer, rounded vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʌ/ is short, central and made with neutral lips; /ɔː/ is long, back and made with clearly rounded lips. Both length and lip shape help you tell them apart.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʌ/ keep the lips relaxed and the jaw barely open. For /ɔː/ round the lips into a circle, pull the tongue back and hold the vowel longer.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare length first, then lip rounding.
quests.explanation: "Walk" lasts longer and the lips are clearly rounded. "Wok" is shorter and more open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare length first: /ɔː/ is held, /ɒ/ is clipped. Then compare colour: /ɔː/ sounds closed and rounded, /ɒ/ sounds open and plain.
quests.mouthPosition: Imagine the shape of an oval mouth for /ɒ/ and a small circle for /ɔː/, then hold the second one longer.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is identical. Listen only to the final consonant.
quests.explanation: It was "face": a sharp, high hiss with the tongue behind the teeth. "Faith" ends with a soft airy sound with the tongue against the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiceless fricatives. The place of the tongue changes the quality of the hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the air flow gentle for /θ/ and focused for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the first sound: hiss or soft friction?
quests.explanation: "Sum" opens with a sharp /s/. "Thumb" opens with a diffuse /θ/ with the tongue at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is made by placing the tongue tip against or between the teeth and blowing air softly; /s/ is made with the tongue behind the teeth and a narrow groove, giving a sharper hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ let the tongue tip touch the edge of the upper teeth and blow gently. For /s/ pull the tongue back behind the teeth and narrow the air channel.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end with a quiet fricative. Where does the friction come from?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "deaf": the lower lip touched the upper teeth. "Death" has the tongue between the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Where the friction happens differs: tongue for /θ/, lip for /f/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue relaxed for /f/; the lips do the work.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the beginning start with a burst?
quests.explanation: "Taught" begins with a burst from the tongue tip. "Thought" begins with a soft flow of air between the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is a fricative with continuous airflow; /t/ is a stop with a complete closure and a burst. Listen for sustained friction versus a sudden release.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ rest the tongue tip against the teeth and let air flow. For /t/ press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth, stop the air, then release.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel. The ending is the only cue.
quests.explanation: You heard "moss": a crisp hiss at the end. "Moth" trails off with a soft airy sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ sounds soft and diffuse; /s/ sounds sharp and high-pitched.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: you should see the tongue tip for /θ/ but not for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are diphthongs. Does the vowel begin rounded or open?
quests.explanation: "Bile" begins wide open and closes with spread lips. "Boil" begins rounded and slides forward.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding at the beginning marks /ɔɪ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'oh' and then slide into 'ee' for /ɔɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two glides ending on schwa. Where does the vowel start?
quests.explanation: The word was "fair": the vowel began half open. "Fear" starts with a tighter, higher vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪə/ starts with the jaw nearly closed; /eə/ starts with the jaw about half open. Both finish with a relaxed schwa.
quests.mouthPosition: Start /ɪə/ in a small smile and let it fall; start /eə/ with a slightly wider mouth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Rounded lips at the start, or a wide-open jaw?
quests.explanation: "Buy" opens the jaw wide first. "Boy" starts with rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔɪ/ starts with rounded lips and a back tongue, while /aɪ/ starts with an open, unrounded mouth. Both end in /ɪ/, so listen to the beginning.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔɪ/ start with clearly rounded lips, then spread them as you glide up. For /aɪ/ begin with the jaw open and the lips neutral.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Do the lips finish round or spread?
quests.explanation: It was "toe": the lips closed toward a round. "Toy" ends with the lips spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The diphthong /ɔɪ/ changes lip shape from round to spread within one syllable; the other vowel does not.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'aw' then 'ee' very close together to get the movement of /ɔɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel and ending are the same. What comes first?
quests.explanation: "Sheep" begins with a smooth hush. "Cheap" begins with a stop that releases into a hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiceless; the stop part is the clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded for both.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the end: does a stop come before the hush?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "bash": a smooth hush with no stop. "Batch" has a stop then a hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a continuous fricative; /tʃ/ begins with a stop and then releases into friction, so it sounds abrupt at the start. Listen for a sudden beginning versus a smooth flow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ let the air flow steadily over the tongue. For /tʃ/ block the air with the tongue against the ridge, then release into a hush.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long vowels in both. Which ending buzzes?
quests.explanation: "Seize" ends with a buzz and the vowel lasts a bit longer. "Cease" ends with a crisp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /z/ lengthens the vowel before it and has a soft buzz; /s/ shortens the vowel and ends with a crisp hiss. In final position the buzz can be weak, so vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the tongue behind the upper teeth. For /s/ end with a sharp hiss after a short vowel; for /z/ stretch the vowel and finish with a softer buzz.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips only, or lip and teeth?
quests.explanation: That was "wheel": the lips rounded and released with no teeth contact. "Veal" buzzes between the lower lip and the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /w/ uses both lips rounded with no contact between lip and teeth; /v/ uses the lower lip against the upper teeth with friction and a buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: For /v/ bite the lower lip lightly with the upper teeth and vibrate. For /w/ round the lips and do not touch the teeth at all.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: First sound: buzzing friction or a lip burst?
quests.explanation: "Vanish" starts with the lip on the teeth and a buzz. "Banish" starts with a lip burst.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The stop /b/ blocks the air completely, /v/ never does.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips close for /b/ but the teeth touch the lip for /v/.
